To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) FLI1 expression in breast cancer is correlated with a better prognosis; 2) FLI1 inhibits cellular growth, migration and invasion of breast cancer cells; 3) FLI1 is down regulated in breast cancer and this may contribute to tumor progression; and 4) FLI1 may regulate expression of genes involved with breast cancer progression.
FLI1 is a tumor suppressor gene that inhibits breast cancer growth, migration, invasion and metastasis.

FLI1 expression inhibits cellular growth, migration and invasion, FLI1 downregulation in breast cancer is correlated with shorter patient survival and more aggressive tumor phenotype and FLI1 is a potential prognostic and therapeutic target.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression, regulation, and function of the ETS factor FLI1 in breast cancer.
the role of ETS factors in breast cancer, and the results presented here suggest that FLI1 may be an important regulator of breast cancer cell growth, migration and invasion.
the identification and characterization of novel genes that may contribute to breast cancer progression.
